title: Universal SNI of an Iterated Mask-Refreshing Gadget
summary: The proposed construction is parallelizable, but strong non-interference for every share count remains unproved and requires either a proof or a counterexample.

formal_statement.body: For the simple mask-refreshing gadget over $d$ shares, determine whether repeating the gadget exactly $\lceil d(d-1)/3 \rceil$ times always produces a mask-refreshing algorithm satisfying $(d-1)$-strong non-interference (SNI) for every $d$. The resulting construction is parallelizable, but strong non-interference for all values of $d$ has not been proved; the unresolved task is therefore to prove this universal claim or provide a counterexample.

scope.domain: Mask refreshing and strong non-interference in side-channel cryptography.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether the stated repetition count always yields a strong non-interference mask-refreshing algorithm for every share count, or whether a counterexample exists.

citations.label: Parallel Implementations of Masking Schemes and the Bounded Moment Leakage Model

progress.summary: The source explicitly presents a conjecture that iterating the simple gadget from Algorithm 1 at the stated count yields a strong non-interference mask-refreshing algorithm over d shares. It notes that the construction is parallelizable and leaves a proof for all d as future work.
citation_labels: Gilles Barthe et al., Parallel Implementations of Masking Schemes and the Bounded Moment Leakage Model
